articles.title: Kettle Hill Gets $7,500 for After-school Reading Program
articles.deck: Residents of Kettle Hill filled the hall on Saturday to ask questions about the plan.
body: Gwen Pelletier, who has lived in Kettle Hill for 19 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. The plan calls for after-school reading program along Cooper Drive, with work expected to start in October.
The group has raised $7,500 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. The Kettle Hill Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.

articles.title: Agnes Thibodeaux, 89, Longtime Volunteer
articles.deck: Friends remember Agnes Thibodeaux for the many years of service to Cedar Hollow.
body: Agnes Thibodeaux died in July at home on Mulberry Road, at the age of 89. Born in Cedar Hollow in the years after the war, Agnes Thibodeaux spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.

Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Cedar Hollow. Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Stonebridge Trail Crew in his or her name.

articles.title: Letter: Support the Book Exchange Box
body: To the editor: I have lived on Sycamore Road for 33 years, and I want to say what a difference the Foundry Row Mutual Aid Group has made. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
Please keep the book exchange box in the budget. Many of us on Sycamore Road use it every week. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the March meeting.
Esther Caruso, Stonebridge

articles.title: Council Approves $850 for Oak Avenue Repairs
articles.deck: Supporters and opponents on Oak Avenue disagreed about cost and timing.
body: The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first.
Public works estimates the work will take about 22 weeks once it starts in April. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

Councilmember Dominic Cifuentes asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $850. Residents of Foundry Row said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.
